To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the drought-induced transcriptional response in leaves is genotype-dependent and that it includes the early activation of sensing and signaling cascades, whereas the response in roots appears to be genotype-independent and is characterized by an activation of sensing and signal transduction pathways, as well as of processes associated with energy production, protein turnover and stress response.

the transcriptional responses in poplar root apices and mature leaves to moderate drought are consistent across genotypes, and that the genotype-dependent component is specific to leaves and includes a developmental component.

(i) the transcriptional response of root apices was consistent across genotypes and treatments, (ii) the transcriptional remodellings of leaves were consistent across treatments, but diverged between the two genotypes, and (iii) the transcriptional differences between the genotypes were more pronounced in the long-term response of the drought-sensitive poplars

the two genotypes are differentially responsive to drought, with the drought-sensitive genotype exhibiting a more pronounced and prolonged transcriptional response in leaves.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptional response in poplar roots to drought is similar to what has been observed in arabidopsis roots.
the drought-induced transcriptomic response of leaves is highly genotype-dependent, whereas that of root apices appears to be largely conserved across species and genotypes.
the transcriptional responses to drought are highly conserved across species, but that genotype-dependent differences in the transcriptome response can be found.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptomic response in poplar leaves is more genotype-dependent than in roots, which may explain why the genotype-dependent component is not as easily detectable in the latter.

a comparative transcriptomics approach can be used to detect the genotype-dependent component in the drought-induced transcriptional response in poplar, and can thus be used for the identification of candidate genes and processes involved in the genetic basis of drought tolerance.
the transcriptional response to drought is a complex and dynamic phenomenon that is strongly genotype-dependent and is likely under developmental control.
